videos.title: How Switzerland Engineered a $90K Per Capita Fortress

By transforming a rugged, landlocked topography into a global vault, they made themselves the world’s ultimate safe house. videos.title: Why Luxembourg is the Richest Nation on Earth

videos.topic: The Secret Financial Machine of Singapore: From Swamp to Superpower
videos.title: How Singapore Built a Trillion-Dollar Financial Fortress
videos.script_preview: In 1965, Singapore was a mosquito-ridden swamp with zero natural resources. Today, it commands the highest per-capita GDP on the planet. The secret? Temasek Holdings. This state-owned behemoth doesn't just manage assets; it owns the nation's infrastructure. It holds controlling stakes in massive bellwether corporations like Singtel, Singapore Airlines, and ST Engineering. While other nations tax for survival, Singapore captures value as the world’s primary entrepôt, refining raw global goods. videos.topic: The Economics of Trillion-Dollar Megaprojects: Saudi Vision 2030
videos.title: The $900B Saudi Exit Strategy
videos.script_preview: Saudi Arabia’s $900 billion Public Investment Fund isn't just a portfolio; it's a high-stakes hedge to secure the regime's future. The PIF manages these assets, yet 75% of Saudi fiscal revenue remains strictly tethered to oil exports. Vision 2030 was launched to pivot this, but the $500 billion Neom project has faced massive scaling back. We are witnessing an autocrat consolidating power by pivoting from a commodity-based economy to a state-controlled conglomerate model. While officials promise innovation, 21,000 deaths on program-related sites underscore the brutal cost of this acceleration.

videos.topic: The Geopolitics of Choke Points: The Battle for the Strait of Malacca
videos.title: Strait of Malacca: The Global Choke Point
videos.script_preview: One narrow ditch holds the entire global economy hostage. The Strait of Malacca. It is the jugular vein of modern trade. Every year, 94,000 ships drag 25% of the world’s global goods and 35% of all seaborne oil through this 1.7-mile wide bottleneck.
